subject: Question about the validity of subsampling repeated measures for MacKenzie-Bailey GOF test....

messages.author: 593c4b97dca6f0d3
messages.subject: Question about the validity of subsampling repeated measures for MacKenzie-Bailey GOF test....
parts:
Dear all, I'm hoping to get some feedback on an approach I'm considering to assess model fit given my somewhat problematic dataset. 

To give a background:

I'm using "unmarked" to model single-season (bird) occupancy at various survey locations that have employed both point counts and audio recording (ARUs). In the analysis I'm interested in what factors impact detection probabilities rather than occupancy. The ARUs have been repeatedly sampled within-day, as we are interested in temporal patterns in detection over the morning (I'm including a temporal auto-correlation term to deal with the proximity of the sampling in time). Due to the design, some sites have >20 repeated measures within season. I want to assess GOF and have been using the MacKenzie and Bailey goodness-of-fit test. The Chi-sq values for some species are mammoth and from my reading I gather that the MacKenzie-Bailey test does not perform well with datasets that have a high ratio of resampling to total survey sites because very rare detection histories become increasingly common and inflate the Chi-sq.  This seems to be what is happening with my output (note the >10,000,000 value):

My question is, can I work around this limitation by reducing the number of repeated measures for the GOF test only? Doing so would mean more cohorts were pooled together. I would use the full dataset for the final models. Right now I've tried this by limiting the data to a maximum of 10 repeated measures per site and this appears to improve the output substantially. I have no reason to assume that the model fit should be different for the later repeated measures but I could potentially randomly sample 10 surveys within-site to deal with that. Thoughts? Also, is there a reason to assume that a c.hat value derived from a truncated dataset is "wrong"?

Many thanks!
